finding.problem: A preview now moves the request to `built` before the kernel has replied with `record_build`. The old `previewing` stage blocked deploy ('The preview has not finished'), and that guard is gone. A re-preview from `built` or `done` leaves the earlier `harness_ok: true` in place, so `deploy` passes `harness-passed` and the `deploying-builds-passed-their-harness` invariant while the new build is still running. That can deploy a build whose harness has not passed. `built` can also now mean a build that has not been recorded.
finding.where: delivery.domain.yaml, transitions.DeliveryRequest: requested/built/done `preview` -> built; `deploy` precondition harness-passed

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: Real consequence of the edit: preview now lands in `built` while `record_build` is still pending, so a stale `harness_ok` can let `deploy` pass, but it is not the seeded stranding of in-flight previewing requests.

finding.problem: `record_build` is still the reply to `preview`, so the preview is not instantaneous. Once `deploy` moves the request on to `deploying` or `done`, a late `record_build` reply hits an `n/a` cell and is dropped or rejected. The build and harness result are never recorded. This contradicts the stated reason that a preview finishes at once.

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: `record_build` remains the reply to `preview`, and in `deploying`/`done` it is `n/a`, so a late reply can be dropped; this is real but not the seeded problem.

finding.problem: The new `built.record_build` cell (to: built) has status `proposed` and no source, so it is an unconfirmed permission-matrix cell introduced by the change. The `built.preview` cell now carries `to: built` under the old interview quote, which was given for a different transition (to previewing).

findings.label: false-alarm
findings.why: Marking a new cell `proposed` is the normal way to flag an unconfirmed cell, and reusing the quote on `built.preview` is not a functional defect.

finding.problem: A stage value is removed from the `DeliveryRequest` enum, and the interface changes (previews no longer pass through `previewing`). The domain `version` stays 1 and the composition still pins interface 1, so consumers cannot tell the interface changed.

findings.label: false-alarm
findings.why: Version bumping is outside the request and is speculative here; it does not identify the stranded previewing objects.

edit.why: It removes the `previewing` enum value and its matrix row, and reroutes `preview` from requested, built and done directly to `built`, so a preview finishes at once.
